methods.label: Distinguish association from a unique output
methods.explanation: A functional relationship assigns exactly one \(y\) to each allowed \(x\). Correlation describes an overall association and need not determine \(y\) exactly. In the linear case illustrated by B, points may scatter around a straight line. Association can also be nonlinear, and correlation can coexist with a function: \(y=x\), with varying \(x\), is an exact function with perfect positive linear correlation. Thus B is the best listed answer, with its straight-line description understood as the linear case.
methods.levelReason: The method compares elementary definitions and uses y=x as a direct example. It requires no correlation formula or advanced statistical theory.

No distinct alternative is useful.
